## Sentiment Analysis

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
library(tidytext)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(textstem)
library(readr)
library(forcats)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
data_e <- read_csv("/Volumes/Thesis/Epstein_Files/output/extraction_combined.csv")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
TEXT_COL <- "text"
ID_COL   <- "file_name"

output_dir <- "/Volumes/Thesis/Epstein_Files/output/sentiment"

doc_sent_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "doc_sentiment_by_dataset_lemma")
word_cnt_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "word_counts_by_dataset_lemma")

dir.create(doc_sent_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(word_cnt_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

bing  <- get_sentiments("bing")
afinn <- get_sentiments("afinn")
nrc   <- get_sentiments("nrc")

redaction_pattern <- regex("\\[[^\\]]*redact[^\\]]*\\]|redact\\w*", ignore_case = TRUE)
```

Word level sentiment, chunked by dataset

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
datasets <- unique(data_e$file_origin)

if (length(datasets) == 0) {
  stop("`datasets` is empty — check that `data_e$file_origin` is the correct column name.")
}

# data-set-9/10/11 are far larger than the rest of the corpus and blew past
# R's 16GB vector memory limit when processed as a single chunk. These get
# processed in smaller in-memory batches, then recombined and written out
# as ONE file per dataset, same as every other dataset -- so the on-disk
# structure and the resume-by-file-existence check are unchanged.
DOC_BATCH_SIZE <- 2000
LARGE_DATASETS <- c("data-set-9-files", "data-set-10-files", "data-set-11-files")

for (i in seq_along(datasets)) {
  ds <- datasets[i]
  message("Word-level sentiment: ", ds, " (", i, "/", length(datasets), ")")
  
  ds_safe <- str_replace_all(ds, "[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_")
  doc_sent_file <- file.path(doc_sent_dir, paste0(ds_safe, ".csv"))
  word_cnt_file <- file.path(word_cnt_dir, paste0(ds_safe, ".csv"))
  
  if (file.exists(doc_sent_file) && file.exists(word_cnt_file)) {
    message("  already done, skipping")
    next
  }
  
  ds_docs <- data_e |>
    filter(file_origin == ds) |>
    select(all_of(c(ID_COL, "file_origin", TEXT_COL))) |>
    arrange(!!sym(ID_COL))
  
  n_docs <- nrow(ds_docs)
  batch_size <- if (ds %in% LARGE_DATASETS) 500 else DOC_BATCH_SIZE
  n_batches <- ceiling(n_docs / batch_size)
  
  doc_sent_list <- vector("list", n_batches)
  word_cnt_list <- vector("list", n_batches)
  
  for (b in seq_len(n_batches)) {
    if (n_batches > 1) message("  batch ", b, "/", n_batches)
    row_start <- (b - 1) * batch_size + 1
    row_end   <- min(b * batch_size, n_docs)
    
    chunk_tokens <- ds_docs[row_start:row_end, ] |>
      mutate(!!TEXT_COL := str_remove_all(!!sym(TEXT_COL), redaction_pattern)) |>
      unnest_tokens(word, !!sym(TEXT_COL))
    
    # lemmatize unique words only, then join back -- avoids re-lemmatizing
    # every duplicate token occurrence, which is what made the large
    # datasets so much more memory-hungry than their doc count alone suggests
    lemma_lookup <- tibble(word = unique(chunk_tokens$word)) |>
      mutate(lemma = lemmatize_words(word))
    
    chunk_tokens <- chunk_tokens |>
      left_join(lemma_lookup, by = "word") |>
      select(-word) |>
      rename(word = lemma)
    
    doc_sent_list[[b]] <- chunk_tokens |>
      inner_join(bing, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
      count(!!sym(ID_COL), file_origin, sentiment)
    
    word_cnt_list[[b]] <- chunk_tokens |>
      inner_join(bing, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
      count(word, sentiment, sort = FALSE)
    
    rm(chunk_tokens, lemma_lookup)
    gc()
  }
  
  rm(ds_docs)
  gc()
  
  # recombine batches back into ONE per-dataset file, matching the
  # original output structure used for every other dataset
  doc_sent <- bind_rows(doc_sent_list) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
  
  if (!"positive" %in% names(doc_sent)) doc_sent$positive <- 0
  if (!"negative" %in% names(doc_sent)) doc_sent$negative <- 0
  doc_sent <- doc_sent |> mutate(sentiment = positive - negative)
  
  write.csv(doc_sent, doc_sent_file, row.names = FALSE)
  
  chunk_word_counts <- bind_rows(word_cnt_list) |>
    group_by(word, sentiment) |>
    summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop")
  
  write.csv(chunk_word_counts, word_cnt_file, row.names = FALSE)
  
  rm(doc_sent_list, word_cnt_list, doc_sent, chunk_word_counts)
  gc()
}

doc_sentiment <- map_dfr(
  list.files(doc_sent_dir, full.names = TRUE),
  read_csv,
  col_types = cols(
    file_name   = col_character(),
    file_origin = col_character(),
    positive    = col_double(),
    negative    = col_double(),
    sentiment   = col_double()
  )
)

word_counts <- map_dfr(
  list.files(word_cnt_dir, full.names = TRUE),
  read_csv,
  col_types = cols(
    word      = col_character(),
    sentiment = col_character(),
    n         = col_double()
  )
) |>
  group_by(word, sentiment) |>
  summarise(n = sum(.data$n), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(n))

saveRDS(doc_sentiment, file.path(output_dir, "doc_sentiment.rds"))
saveRDS(word_counts, file.path(output_dir, "word_counts.rds"))
```

Most common positive and negative words

```{r}
#| echo: false

word_counts |>
  group_by(sentiment) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 20) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(word = reorder(word, n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, word, fill = sentiment)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~sentiment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Contribution to sentiment", y = NULL,
       title = "Most common sentiment-bearing words in the disclosures corpus")

word_counts |> filter(sentiment == "negative") |> slice_max(n, n = 30) |> print(n = 30)
word_counts |> filter(sentiment == "positive") |> slice_max(n, n = 30) |> print(n = 30)
```

Sentiment distributions in datasets

```{r}
#| echo: false

doc_sentiment_rds <- file.path(output_dir, "doc_sentiment.rds")

doc_sent_source_files <- list.files(doc_sent_dir, full.names = TRUE)
rds_is_current <- file.exists(doc_sentiment_rds) &&
  length(doc_sent_source_files) > 0 &&
  file.info(doc_sentiment_rds)$mtime > max(file.info(doc_sent_source_files)$mtime)

if (rds_is_current) {
  doc_sentiment <- readRDS(doc_sentiment_rds)
} else {
  doc_sentiment <- map_dfr(
    doc_sent_source_files,
    read_csv,
    col_types = cols(
      file_name   = col_character(),
      file_origin = col_character(),
      positive    = col_double(),
      negative    = col_double(),
      sentiment   = col_double()
    )
  )
  saveRDS(doc_sentiment, doc_sentiment_rds)
}

chunk_size <- 200  # documents per chunk

dataset_sentiment <- doc_sentiment |>
  arrange(file_origin, file_name) |>
  group_by(file_origin) |>
  mutate(index = (row_number() - 1) %/% chunk_size) |>
  group_by(file_origin, index) |>
  summarise(
    positive = sum(positive),
    negative = sum(negative),
    sentiment = positive - negative,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

saveRDS(dataset_sentiment, file.path(output_dir, "dataset_sentiment.rds"))

# split datasets by whether they have enough chunks to plot meaningfully
chunk_counts <- dataset_sentiment |> count(file_origin, name = "n_chunks")

plottable   <- chunk_counts |> filter(n_chunks >= 5) |> pull(file_origin) |> sort()
too_small   <- chunk_counts |> filter(n_chunks < 5) |> pull(file_origin)

# split the plottable datasets into two roughly equal halves so each
# trajectory plot shows ~6 panels instead of all of them crammed onto
# one screen
half_point   <- ceiling(length(plottable) / 2)
plottable_1  <- plottable[seq_len(half_point)]
plottable_2  <- plottable[(half_point + 1):length(plottable)]

# trajectory plot, part 1 — first half of datasets with enough chunks
dataset_sentiment |>
  filter(file_origin %in% plottable_1) |>
  ggplot(aes(index, sentiment, fill = file_origin)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~file_origin, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = paste0("Chunk (", chunk_size, " documents each)"),
       y = "Net sentiment (positive − negative)",
       title = "Sentiment distribution across datasets (1 of 2)")

# trajectory plot, part 2 — second half of datasets with enough chunks
dataset_sentiment |>
  filter(file_origin %in% plottable_2) |>
  ggplot(aes(index, sentiment, fill = file_origin)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~file_origin, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = paste0("Chunk (", chunk_size, " documents each)"),
       y = "Net sentiment (positive − negative)",
       title = "Sentiment distribution across datasets (2 of 2)")

# simple summary for the too-small ones instead
doc_sentiment |>
  filter(file_origin %in% too_small) |>
  group_by(file_origin) |>
  summarise(total_sentiment = sum(sentiment), n_docs = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

Comparing Lexicons across dataset 11

```{r}
#| echo: false

chunk_size <- 200  # same as your dataset-level plot, for consistency

# ============================================================================
# Tokenize + lemmatize data-set-11-files once, reuse for all three lexicons
# ============================================================================

ds11_tokens <- data_e |>
  filter(file_origin == "data-set-11-files") |>
  select(all_of(c(ID_COL, "file_origin", TEXT_COL))) |>
  arrange(!!sym(ID_COL)) |>
  mutate(doc_index = (row_number() - 1) %/% chunk_size) |>  # assign chunk before unnesting
  mutate(!!TEXT_COL := str_remove_all(!!sym(TEXT_COL), redaction_pattern)) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, !!sym(TEXT_COL)) |>
  mutate(word = lemmatize_words(word))

# ============================================================================
# AFINN — sum of values per chunk
# ============================================================================

afinn_ds11 <- ds11_tokens |>
  inner_join(afinn, by = "word") |>
  group_by(index = doc_index) |>
  summarise(sentiment = sum(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(method = "AFINN")

# ============================================================================
# Bing + NRC — positive/negative counts per chunk
# ============================================================================

bing_and_nrc_ds11 <- bind_rows(
  ds11_tokens |>
    inner_join(bing, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    mutate(method = "Bing et al."),
  ds11_tokens |>
    inner_join(
      nrc |> filter(sentiment %in% c("positive", "negative")),
      by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many"
    ) |>
    mutate(method = "NRC")
) |>
  count(method, index = doc_index, sentiment) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative)

# ============================================================================
# Combine and plot
# ============================================================================

bind_rows(afinn_ds11, bing_and_nrc_ds11) |>
  ggplot(aes(index, sentiment, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~method, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = paste0("Chunk (", chunk_size, " documents each)"),
    y = "Net sentiment",
    title = "Lexicon comparison — data-set-11-files"
  )
```

TF-IDF

```{r}
#| echo: false

# ============================================================================
# 1. Word counts per dataset, chunked and cleaned the same way as the LDA pipeline
# ============================================================================

alpha_only_pattern <- r"(^[a-z]+$)"  # kills numbers, punctuation, mixed tokens

structural_words <- c(
  # plist/xml artifacts
  "xml", "plist", "dtd", "dtds", "doctype", "propertylist", "dict", "key", "array",
  "integer", "string", "flag", "apple", "public",
  # email header/timestamp artifacts
  "date", "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "send", "monday", "tuesday",
  "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "subject", "begin", "forward",
  "conversation", "pm", "am", "gmail", "remote", "id", "receive", "view",
  "write", "original", "message", "encode", "utf", "sit", "sat", "sun"
)

word_count_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "tfidf_word_counts_by_dataset_clean")
dir.create(word_count_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

datasets <- unique(data_e$file_origin)
if (length(datasets) == 0) stop("`datasets` is empty — check file_origin column.")

for (i in seq_along(datasets)) {
  ds <- datasets[i]
  ds_safe <- str_replace_all(ds, "[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_")
  out_file <- file.path(word_count_dir, paste0(ds_safe, ".csv"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_file)) { message(ds, " already done, skipping"); next }
  message("Counting words: ", ds, " (", i, "/", length(datasets), ")")
  
  ds_docs <- data_e |>
    filter(file_origin == ds) |>
    select(all_of(c(ID_COL, "file_origin", TEXT_COL))) |>
    arrange(!!sym(ID_COL))
  
  n_docs <- nrow(ds_docs)
  batch_size <- if (ds %in% LARGE_DATASETS) 500 else DOC_BATCH_SIZE
  n_batches <- ceiling(n_docs / batch_size)
  
  word_count_list <- vector("list", n_batches)
  
  for (b in seq_len(n_batches)) {
    if (n_batches > 1) message("  batch ", b, "/", n_batches)
    row_start <- (b - 1) * batch_size + 1
    row_end   <- min(b * batch_size, n_docs)
    
    chunk_tokens <- ds_docs[row_start:row_end, ] |>
      mutate(!!TEXT_COL := str_remove_all(!!sym(TEXT_COL), redaction_pattern)) |>
      unnest_tokens(word, !!sym(TEXT_COL))
    
    lemma_lookup <- tibble(word = unique(chunk_tokens$word)) |>
      mutate(lemma = lemmatize_words(word))
    
    word_count_list[[b]] <- chunk_tokens |>
      left_join(lemma_lookup, by = "word") |>
      select(-word) |>
      rename(word = lemma) |>
      filter(
        str_detect(word, alpha_only_pattern),
        nchar(word) <= 20,
        !word %in% stop_words$word,
        !word %in% structural_words
      ) |>
      count(file_origin, word, sort = FALSE)
    
    rm(chunk_tokens, lemma_lookup)
    gc()
  }
  
  rm(ds_docs)
  gc()
  
  chunk_words <- bind_rows(word_count_list) |>
    group_by(file_origin, word) |>
    summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop")
  
  write.csv(chunk_words, out_file, row.names = FALSE)
  
  rm(word_count_list, chunk_words)
  gc()
}

# ============================================================================
# 2. Combine into one dataframe
# ============================================================================

dataset_words <- map_dfr(
  list.files(word_count_dir, full.names = TRUE),
  read_csv,
  col_types = cols(file_origin = col_character(), word = col_character(), n = col_double())
) |>
  group_by(file_origin, word) |>
  summarise(n = sum(.data$n), .groups = "drop")

saveRDS(dataset_words, file.path(output_dir, "dataset_words_clean.rds"))

# ============================================================================
# 3. bind_tf_idf
# ============================================================================

dataset_tf_idf <- dataset_words |>
  bind_tf_idf(word, file_origin, n)

saveRDS(dataset_tf_idf, file.path(output_dir, "dataset_tf_idf_clean.rds"))

dataset_tf_idf |>
  arrange(desc(tf_idf)) |>
  slice_head(n = 50)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# 4. Plot — one graph per dataset, 12 total
# ============================================================================

top_words <- dataset_tf_idf |>
  group_by(file_origin) |>
  slice_max(tf_idf, n = 10) |>
  ungroup()

for (ds in sort(unique(top_words$file_origin))) {
  p <- top_words |>
    filter(file_origin == ds) |>
    ggplot(aes(tf_idf, fct_reorder(word, tf_idf))) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue", show.legend = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "tf-idf", y = NULL, title = paste0("Most distinctive words — ", ds))
  
  print(p)
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path("/Volumes/Thesis/plots", paste0("topic_", ds, ".png")),
    plot = p,
    width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300
  )
}
```
